29334.explanation: The Nigerian Youth Movement (NYM) was founded in 1936. It was a political organization that emerged during the colonial period in Nigeria, with the aim of advocating for the interests of the youth and promoting nationalist ideals. The movement played a significant role in the political landscape of Nigeria in the pre-independence era. The organization operated at a time when various groups were actively engaged in discussions about the future political structure of Nigeria. The NYM's formation and activities reflected the growing awareness and political consciousness among the youth in Nigeria during that period.

29342.question_text: The main goals of colonial administration in Nigeria weer the
29342.explanation:
The primary goals of colonial administration in Nigeria were to ensure political control and economic exploitation. The colonial government focused on:

  • Maintaining law and order to secure colonial rule
  • Ensuring efficient extraction and export of raw materials (economic exploitation)
  • Protecting British economic and political interests

This reflects the true nature of colonial rule as primarily exploitative rather than developmental.

options.text: industrialization and expansion of the economy
preservation and protection of traditional heritage
maintenance of law, order and exploitation of the national wealth
introduction and protectional of human rights

29343.subject: Government
29343.question_text: The 1958 Constitutional Conferences responded to the fears of minorities by recommending the
29343.explanation:
The 1958 Constitutional Conference was convened as part of Nigeria’s journey toward independence. One of the major issues raised, especially by minority groups, was the fear of domination by the majority ethnic groups in the existing regions (North, West, and East).

To address these fears, the conference recommended the entrenchment of fundamental human rights in the constitution.
This was intended to protect minority groups from discrimination and ensure their rights were safeguarded regardless of which region they lived in.

29346.subject: Government
29346.question_text: In order to qualify for membership of the House of Representatives in Nigeria, a citizen must have attained the age of
29346.explanation:
Under the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, the minimum age required to contest for membership of the House of Representatives of Nigeria is 25 years.

Originally, the constitution required 30 years. However, this was reduced after the Not Too Young To Run Act was passed in 2018 under the administration of President Muhammadu Buhari, which amended parts of the constitution to allow younger Nigerians to run for public office.

According to the amendment:

  • President – 35 years

  • Senator – 35 years

  • House of Representatives – 25 years

  • State House of Assembly – 25 years

Therefore, to qualify for election into the House of Representatives of Nigeria, a Nigerian citizen must be at least 25 years old.
